clue.text: Shining example of a famous "film noir"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lamp that burns town gas, an example of something that shines
second meaning: the 1944 psychological thriller starring Ingrid Bergman

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a celebrated dark movie as a brilliant model of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shining example' reads as praise for the film, but it is a literal description of a gas lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas lamps lit Victorian streets and homes, and the same word titles a classic dark thriller about psychological manipulation.

clue.text: Dress adds vitality to a heartless woman

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle of the word is cut out, leaving only its ends

parts.note: go means energy or vitality, as in 'full of go'
the word woman with its middle letters taken out

explanation.surface: A dress brings energy and life to a cold, unfeeling woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown is a long formal garment, a kind of dress worn by women on special occasions.

clue.text: Only a flatfish

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a flat sea fish such as the Dover variety

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that it is merely a flatfish, nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means single or exclusive, and the noun names a common flat seabed fish eaten widely in Europe.

clue.text: I'm needing white stick

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
pale means white or colourless

explanation.surface: A blind person explains they require a white cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White stick' is the cane carried by a blind person, but 'stick' here is a verb, to pierce.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something through with a sharp point is to stick it, as on a stake or spike.

clue.text: Card game for merry households

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a children's game collecting four members of illustrated families such as Mr Bun the Baker
second meaning: read literally, cheerful domestic groups

explanation.surface: A card game recommended for cheerful homes.
explanation.walkthrough: Happy Families is a traditional British children's card game played with a special illustrated pack.
explanation.definitionFit: The game's name, read word by word, describes cheerful households, so both readings fit the same phrase.

clue.text: Dog show returns for a second time with fur getting cold

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A canine exhibition comes back again, with animals' coats feeling chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: S, T, FUR and C are lined up and then the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Crufts is the famous annual British dog show held in Birmingham, the largest of its kind in the world.

clue.text: Artist in autumn precipitation

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
taken as written
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A painter out in the wet weather of autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts the artist inside autumn, but it is simply taken as its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain, sleet and snow are all precipitation, and the amount of rain that comes down is measured as the total that falls.

clue.text: Rub shoulders, which could lead to arrest and fine

indicators.note: the letters could lead to something else, so they are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
joins the two pieces of fodder

explanation.surface: Mixing with the wrong crowd might end in being detained and penalised.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub shoulders is an idiom for mixing socially with others, which is exactly what this verb means.

clue.text: Antirrhinum shoot wanted by bossy woman

parts.note: to snap is to shoot a photograph
a dragon is a fierce, domineering woman

explanation.surface: A domineering woman wants a cutting of a garden flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a plant's new growth beside the flower, but it means take a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: Antirrhinum is the botanical genus name of the garden flower whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed.

clue.text: Women all getting journal with something on interiors

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
taken as written
a journal is a newspaper

explanation.surface: Every woman buys a home-decorating magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something on interiors' sounds like a magazine topic, but it means a covering put on indoor walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterned sheets pasted onto room walls are literally a thing applied to the inside surfaces of a house.

clue.text: Clobber required: stretch girdles and skirt

parts.note: a run is a stretch, as in a run of luck
to girdle is to encircle, or ring
to skirt something is to go round it

explanation.surface: A shopping list of clothing: stretchy fabric, corsets and a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for clothes, which the surface plays on, but here it is a verb meaning to beat soundly.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber an opponent is to defeat them heavily, and the idiom means to outperform someone with ease.

clue.text: I have a North American girl coming from Russia

parts.note: the contraction I've, written as its sounded letters without the silent E
taken as written
NA is the abbreviation for North American

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have an American girlfriend arriving from Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivana is a Slavic girl's name, common in Russia and Eastern Europe, so it names a woman from there.

clue.text: Paying about a pound to get participants a pitch

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

parts.note: taken as written
L is the symbol for a pound sterling, from Latin libra
the field is all those taking part in a race or contest

explanation.surface: Handing over a pound so the players can use a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside PAYING after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch is a sports ground marked out for games such as football or cricket, an outdoor area for play.

clue.text: Firstly, I'm pregnant!

parts.note: surface reading: a woman leading off a conversation with her big news
setter's reading: a woman expecting her first child is not yet a parent, but one in waiting

explanation.surface: A woman opens her announcement with the news of a coming baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firstly' seems to order the announcement; it really points to a first baby, making the speaker a parent only in prospect.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman expecting a baby is described with this hyphenated phrase, a future parent awaiting the birth.

clue.text: Saint Thomas in agony when standing

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for saint
Tom is the short form of Thomas
something aching is in pain

explanation.surface: A saint suffering torment while kept upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saint' usually gives ST, but here only S is used, since the T starts Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing something means putting up with it, and to stomach a thing is likewise to tolerate it.

clue.text: A vow taken in the boathouse

indicators.note: what is taken in is held within, so the letters sit inside a longer word

parts.note: the word sits inside this longer one

explanation.surface: A promise made inside the riverside shed where boats are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise, such as one sworn in court or at a coronation, is a vow.

clue.text: Star of "The Great Caruso" was, surprisingly, a moral Nazi

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shocking claim that a famous film star was a principled fascist.
explanation.definitionFit: The American tenor played the opera singer Enrico Caruso in the 1951 Hollywood biopic, his best-known role.

clue.text: Dagger found in street toilet that is out of order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: something out of order is disarranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A weapon is discovered in a broken public lavatory on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of order' reads naturally as a broken toilet, but it tells you to rearrange its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short knife with a slender tapering blade, a type of dagger.

clue.text: Holds up a poor actor in need of qualifications

parts.note: a ham is a bad, overacting performer
strings are conditions or qualifications attached to an offer

explanation.surface: A bad actor stalls because he lacks the proper credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamstring someone is to cripple or hinder them, so the verb in the third person means holds up or hampers.

clue.text: Capital's very large: see!

parts.note: OS means outsize, a clothing label for very large
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how huge a capital city is.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway, its seat of government on a fjord in the south.

clue.text: Noisy bedfellow's more sensitive around noon

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word is wrapped about another

parts.note: sorer means more tender or painful
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A loud partner in bed becomes touchier towards midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes loud breathing sounds while asleep is a classically noisy partner to share a bed with.

clue.text: Disobedient, making clatter in car

indicators.note: making means forming or building, so the following letters are made into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unruly child kicking up a racket in the back of the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A recalcitrant person stubbornly resists authority or control, so the adjective describes someone who will not obey.

clue.text: Hope to hide a million, which is mine

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: Bob is the first name of the comedian Bob Hope
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to stash away a million pounds that belongs to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mine' reads as a possessive, but it is the explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is an explosive device buried or floating, which is a kind of bomb.

clue.text: Kelly's basic unit of inheritance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the first name of the dancer and actor of Singin' in the Rain
second meaning: the stretch of DNA passed from parent to child

explanation.surface: A description of a Kelly family's fundamental inherited trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Gene Kelly was the Hollywood dancing star, and the biological term names the hereditary unit carried on chromosomes.

clue.text: I study backstreet poet

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the words before it are read from the end

parts.note: taken as written
to do a subject is to study it, as in doing French
the street part of this word gives ST, its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A poet says they read in a back alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backstreet' looks like one word but splits into back, the reversal signal, and street.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist is a writer of odes, lyric poems addressed to a subject, so the word names a kind of poet.

clue.text: Starting point for old-fashioned individual

parts.note: a square is someone conventional or out of date
one means a single person

explanation.surface: Where to begin when dealing with someone stuck in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Going back to the beginning is an idiom, from a board game's first square, for restarting from the very start.

clue.text: Flip me! Vanished to capture two Germans retreating!

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the result is read from the end
capturing something holds it inside, so one word goes within another

parts.note: gone means vanished
G is the abbreviation for German, twice over

explanation.surface: A cry of escape as two Germans are seized and pull back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip me!' has the drink speaking, as if saying 'I am a flip'; G for German comes from the international car code.
explanation.definitionFit: A flip is an old mixed drink of spirits or beer beaten with egg and sugar, the same family as this creamy festive drink.

clue.text: Queen goes to a party, clever and charming

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration
R for Regina, Latin for queen
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: The monarch attends a gathering and proves smart and delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen goes to, that is follows, 'a party', so R comes after A and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adorable is so delightful it inspires affection, which is to say charming.
